title: GOP Operative vs. Mexico – Soberanía 126
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
In episode 126 of Soberanía, hosts José Luis Granados Ceja and Kurt Hackbarth
open with the Senate's approval of the dual nationality reform, which bars
anyone with more than one citizenship from serving as president or governor.
The hosts dismantle the criticism from Larry Rubin — a Republican operative
and president of the American Society of Mexico — who went to the Senate to
lobby against the measure, claiming it discriminates against migrants. The
hosts note the hypocrisy: these same voices have been silent on ICE abuses,
hunger strikes in detention centers, and efforts to make it easier for
migrants to vote.

Next, they examine new revelations in the Cerimedo scandal, including photos
of the far-right operative with Donald Trump Jr., Brad Parscale, and other
right-wing figures. They discuss how Bolivia's attorney general—investigating
Cerimedo's alleged drug ties and assassination plot—has been targeted with
U.S. visa restrictions. Is this an act of retaliation? The hosts connect this
to the broader U.S. strategy of using "narco-terrorist" designations to go
after political opponents across the region, including Colombian Senator Iván
Cepeda, who warns he could be next.

The conversation then turns to Brazil's presidential election, where Lula and
Flávio Bolsonaro are locked in a tight race. The hosts highlight leaked
documents suggesting Bolsonaro's campaign may have offered the U.S. access to
critical minerals in exchange for support, and note that Meta suspended Lula's
paid advertisements days before the vote. They also discuss late-stage
scandals plaguing Bolsonaro, including reports of sex parties, a suspicious
Rolex, and a bizarre biopic starring Jim Caviezel.

Losers and Haters takes aim at the New York Times for a story claiming Andrés
Manuel López Beltrán is seen as the "heir" to AMLO — a claim the hosts say is
completely fabricated and reveals how out of touch the paper is with Mexican
politics.
